instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Put a large pot of water on to boil for the noodles.
In a large bowl, stir the 1/3 cup panko into 3 tbsp milk and let it sit for 3 minutes.

Mince the 2 garlic cloves and chop 2 tbsp of the parsley. Add the turkey, egg, garlic, 1 tbsp of the parsley, 1/4 tsp allspice, 1/4 tsp nutmeg, 1/4 tsp onion powder, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper to the bowl.
Mix with your hands until it just comes together. Stop as soon as there are no streaks left. Any longer and the meatballs come out dense.

Roll the mixture into 1 inch balls, about 20 in all, and set them on the baking sheet. Bake for 15 to 17 minutes. You're cooking them to 165°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left.
While the meatballs bake, melt the 2 tbsp butter in a large, deep skillet over medium heat. Whisk in the 2 tbsp flour and cook for 1 minute, until it smells a little toasty.

Pour in the 2 cups broth a splash at a time, whisking until smooth. Whisk in the 1 tbsp Worcestershire, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1/2 tsp Dijon. Simmer for 5 minutes, whisking now and then, until it coats the back of a spoon.
When the sauce is simmering, add the 8 oz noodles and 2 tsp salt to the boiling water. Cook as the package says, usually 6 to 8 minutes, then drain.

Take the skillet off the heat and stir in the 2/3 cup sour cream. Add the meatballs and any juices from the sheet, and spoon the sauce over them. Put the skillet back on low heat for 2 minutes, until hot. Don't let it boil.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the noodles with the remaining 1 tbsp parsley on top.
method_notes: Platings and Pairings' turkey Swedish meatballs lead (4.74 from 26): turkey meatballs seasoned with allspice and nutmeg, baked, then simmered in a butter and flour gravy with broth, Worcestershire, soy, Dijon and sour cream. Changes: the panko is soaked in a little milk (A Mind Full Mom and Carmyy also use milk) so the lean turkey stays tender, and full sour cream replaces reduced-fat. Egg noodles are added as the base. Lingonberry jam, which the lead lists as optional, is left out.
